text:
maya: hi folks :wave: I'm onboarding this week and need to get secrets set up for the new service `recommendation-api` (dev -> staging -> prod). Who do I ping for Vault paths + KMS key access? I also want to understand rotation responsibilities.
eli: @maya welcome! For secrets you usually file a request via the infra secrets form. That'll auto-create a ticket and set up the Vault path with an owner. Link: https://secrets.redwood.internal/new
sam: pinging infra on your behalf — generally we need the service name, environments, scopes (read/write), and the key usage. Example minimal request in the form:

```
service: recommendation-api
envs: [dev, staging, prod]
scopes:
  - secrets.read
  - secrets.write
kms:
  - usage: encryption
owner: maya
rotation_days: 90
```

sam: the form will add `team:` tags if you pick the owning team so infra knows who to CC. Also set `rotation_days` if you want a non-default schedule.
tara: quick note on KMS: prod keys require an audit approval. If you need a new key, mention the business justification and expected traffic. It usually takes 1-2 business days for provisioning and policy attachments.
maya: thanks — who is the right person to be owner for the service? I'm on the ML infra squad but the product team also touches the service.
eli: make yourself the initial owner if you will rotate/manage creds. We can add the product alias as co-owner. Owners are expected to approve rotation PRs and review access requests.
devex-bot: :robot_face: FYI — there's a Slack workflow `/request-secret` you can run to pre-fill the form. It also adds the ticket to #eng-infra for review.
maya: perfect, I'll submit the form now. One last q: emergency unseal/urgent access flow — who do we call after hours?
sam: after hours, call the oncall engineer (+1-555-0100) and @eng-infra on Slack. There's also a short emergency checklist in the docs: https://internal.redwood/docs/secrets/emergency-access
maya: awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup: I'll post the request link here when submitted so you can review the ticket.
eli: sounds good — tag me if you want a quick review before you hit submit.
